hypothesis: The earlier explicit-shuffle and native-warp-reduction candidates both passed the displayed cases and had repeated reported means below baseline, but those full-program results do not establish that the local tree caused the difference. This contrasting variant retains shuffle reduction within each warp and tests whether a lane-0 serial combine of four warp totals is preferable to a second warp reduction.
notes: The 908efebec59a4521-h01 development attempt failed to build or exceeded its timeout; the available diagnostic does not identify which. Its h02 was marked development_valid and correct, but had no timing. The measured 908efebec59a4521 candidate passed 10 cases (n=1, 127, 1024, 65536, 4194304; two seeds), with guards intact and input unchanged; its three reported samples were 30.7674, 30.0762, and 30.0403 μs (mean 30.2946 μs). The f5b882300c2342ad candidate likewise passed 10 displayed cases; samples were 29.8016, 29.6538, and 29.2666 μs (mean 29.5740 μs). The baseline samples were 46.5651, 46.0806, and 46.0864 μs (mean 46.2441 μs). No supplied correctness cases exercise n=0. This proposal handles n<=0 by asynchronously zeroing output, uses unsigned modulo-2^32 sums with a signed representative conversion that stays in range, and preserves the tile, recursive stages, scratch offsets, ABI, and default-stream operations. This proposed variant has not yet been measured or controller-validated; no correctness result or timing is claimed for it.
transformations: Replace the modulo/shared-memory tree with a five-step warp shuffle reduction, one shared unsigned partial per warp, and a lane-0 serial sum of the four warp totals.

Use unsigned modulo-2^32 arithmetic for all reduction stages; map each stored residue to an in-range signed int via a 64-bit intermediate so conversion is defined, and recover the residue by the standard signed-to-unsigned modulo conversion on the next stage.
Retain zero-filled tail handling, 128-thread blocks, recursive host launches, scratch-bank offsets, ABI, and default-stream ordering; asynchronously zero the output for n<=0.
